judgement: TRUE original echo TCP and UDP packets traversed the high prio child in B: 503 packets, no qdisc child drops, while 3,587,577 bulk packets traversed the low child. The kernel service-order change is not a no-op.

Despite real priority, the true original client's shared source rejected 67 of343 sparse TCP first fragments in B, vs 56 of341 and 50 of263 in original A and A-prime. No evidence of improved local sparse admission.
TCP small-flow p99 B 618ms vs A 368ms and A-prime 2370ms shows substantial drift; no causal positive or stable negative p99 claim can be inferred from single A/B/A-prime, but screen fails.

Receiver goodput preserved within ~1% and CPU/GiB up <2%; this does not offset missing sparse QoS improvement. No general app-port prioritization is acceptable for product, and no production scheduler/default changed.
Next hypothesis must distinguish source-side same-lease M1 admission capacity and service order from kernel qdisc order, not blindly increase 32-record M4 batch or resurrect H2254 rejected eviction.
